source_signature.notes: Batch 4J skill 3/5. Owns obtaining truss member forces by passing an imaginary CUT through the truss and isolating one side as a RIGID BODY. Unlike a joint, a cut portion carries THREE independent equations - SigmaFx = 0, SigmaFy = 0, SigmaM = 0 - so at most three unknown member forces can be resolved by one section. Owns CUT SELECTION (the cut must pass through the wanted members and expose no more than three unknowns) and STRATEGIC MOMENT-POINT SELECTION (taking moments about the point where two unknowns intersect isolates the third in a single equation). Boundary: truss_support_reactions (signed, skill 1) determines the external reactions; the artifact carries the complement - Ax, Ay and Gy are GIVEN and not re-derived. method_of_joints (signed, skill 2) obtains the same quantity by isolating one joint at a time, a particle with two equations, and must propagate joint to joint; that skill names this one as a different method for the same quantity and this artifact states the COMPLEMENT - a section isolates a rigid body with three equations and reaches a member DIRECTLY without solving the joints before it, with 'do not solve joint by joint' authored into the procedure rather than left implicit. rigid_body_equilibrium_2d (signed) supplies the three-equation rigid-body method and is the analogue for a section exactly as particle equilibrium was the analogue for a joint - cited, not re-taught. simple_truss_modeling (signed) supplies the idealisation. member_tension_compression_signs (batch sibling, position 4, not yet signed) owns the tension/compression sign CONVENTION and its cross-method consistency; this skill USES it - assume tension, the cut force pulls the isolated portion toward the removed side - and names the sibling as owner, a forward cession matching the one made by method_of_joints. zero_force_members excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived and independently recomputed: joints A(0,0) pin, D(4,0), E(8,0), G(12,0) on the bottom chord and B(4,3), F(8,3) on the top; nine members, m = 2j - 3 = 9, determinate; loads 6 kN down at D and 24 kN down at E; reactions given Ax = 0, Ay = 12 kN up, Gy = 18 kN up. A vertical cut through BF, DF and DE exposes exactly three unknowns; the left portion (A, B, D) is isolated. SigmaM about D isolates F_BF because F_DF and F_DE both pass through D: -48 - 3 F_BF = 0 -> F_BF = -16 kN (16 kN COMPRESSION). SigmaM about F isolates F_DE because F_BF and F_DF both pass through F: -96 + 24 + 3 F_DE = 0 -> F_DE = +24 kN (24 kN TENSION). SigmaFy isolates F_DF because the other two are horizontal: 12 - 6 + 0.6 F_DF = 0 -> F_DF = -10 kN (10 kN COMPRESSION). Distinguishing feature bites: DIRECT ACCESS is demonstrated with evidence rather than asserted - joint member counts are A 2, B 3, D 4, E 3, F 4, G 2, so reaching DF by method of joints requires THREE joints (A then B then D, or G then E then F) while one section reaches it directly; the cut exposes exactly three unknowns, enough to need all three equations but not so many that the section is unsolvable; both moment points do real work, each isolating a single unknown in one equation rather than requiring a simultaneous solve; and tension and compression both appear. HONEST LIMITATION recorded in concept, procedure, solution and common_errors: once two moment equations and one force equation have been used on a portion, the remaining force equation on that SAME portion is a linear consequence of them - it confirms arithmetic but supplies no independent equilibrium information. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays and is taken on the OTHER portion (joints E, F, G), which brings in Gy = 18 kN and the 24 kN load, neither of which appeared in the left-portion solve: F_BF gives (+16, 0), F_DF gives (+8, +6), F_DE gives (-24, 0), so SigmaFx = 16 + 8 - 24 = 0 and SigmaFy = 18 - 24 + 6 = 0. The artifact notes that SigmaFx on the left portion also closes at zero but is not independent. THREE-signal mapping with chained triggers: sign_or_placement_error at step 3 (the tension assumption - a cut force pulls the isolated portion toward the removed side and acts oppositely on the other portion; its trigger opens by stipulating a valid cut has been selected), axis_confusion at step 4 (component resolution of the diagonal cut force and moment-arm pairing; its trigger opens by stipulating the tension sense is correct), unclassified at step 7 (report and boundary). solution_sequencing_error OMITTED with an explicit contrast against method_of_joints, where it was earned: there, beginning at a three-unknown joint writes two equations against three unknowns and strands them; here the three rigid-body equations are independent and may be written in any order, so choosing a moment point that isolates one unknown is an efficiency choice rather than a stranding. Cutting through four or more unknown members is a CUT-SELECTION error, not a solve-order error, and is routed to unclassified rather than force-fit to sequencing. simple_average_used omitted (Centroids-family). Trig-resolution cross-check N/A recorded affirmatively: member directions follow from joint coordinates and no inclined vector is decomposed from a stated angle. No archetype is asserted while PROCEDURE-ARCHETYPE-LIBRARY-V1 remains unapproved. Operator observation recorded, not corrected: two distinct error classes - cutting through more than three unknown members, and treating a same-portion force check as independent - both route to unclassified because the canonical vocabulary cannot name either; this is a further instance of the signal-vocabulary gap already recorded independently by two Wave 1 windows and is surfaced for the pending taxonomy ruling, with no new signal proposed here. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane.
